learner.background: B.Tech Petroleum Engineering graduate transitioning into AI Engineering
starting_knowledge: practical exposure to APIs, LLM apps, RAG and agentic workflows

A.name: Sequential
A.description: Phases 1 to 13 in order. Deepest understanding, slowest path to a portfolio.

B.name: Just-in-time maths
B.description: Phase 1, then 4, 5, 6, 7 onward. Phases 2 and 3 are taken when a prerequisite edge demands them, which the prerequisite graph enforces automatically.

mastery_policy.description: A topic may be set to done only when all four conditions hold. Status is never evidence; evidence is evidence.
conditions: evidence.exercise.passed is true, recorded from a real pytest run
evidence.quiz.percent is at least the phase threshold, with no critical conceptual error
evidence.explanation.rating is at least 2 on the 0 to 3 scale
no unresolved critical entry in tracker/mistakes.md for this topic

explanation_rating_scale.3: explains and predicts behaviour in a new situation

progress_policy.topic_completion: count of topics with status done divided by total topic count
progress_policy.effort_weighted: sum of estimated_minutes for topics with status done divided by sum of estimated_minutes for all topics
progress_policy.phase_status_rule: Derived, never hand-edited. If any topic is needs_revision the phase is needs_revision; else if all topics are done the phase is done; else if any topic is done or in_progress the phase is in_progress; else not_started. build_roadmap.py recomputes and writes this back.

review_policy.on_correct: advance to the next interval in the list
review_policy.on_partial: repeat the current interval and record the uncertainty
review_policy.note: curriculum.json holds review policy only. All mutable review dates and history live in tracker/review_schedule.json so that structure and state have one owner each.

attribution.note: Topic structure only. No roadmap artwork, styling or descriptive text was copied.

source_values.official: Topic verified present in the official roadmap.sh AI Engineer roadmap
source_values.user: Topic from the learner's own proposed curriculum, not in the official roadmap
source_values.recommended: Topic added on the mentor's recommendation

projects.name: DocMind
projects.summary: Hybrid-retrieval RAG assistant. Existing project, to be measured and upgraded.

projects.name: VINI AI
projects.summary: Voice assistant. Existing project, to be measured and upgraded.

projects.name: Self-Distilling Payment Recovery Agent
projects.summary: Agentic failed-payment triage and recovery. Existing project, to be made reliable and measurable. Mock providers only.

projects.name: AutoBI
projects.summary: CSV-to-dashboard application. Existing project, to be hardened and evaluated.

projects.name: Bounded Research or Coding Agent

phases.title: Programming and Software Foundations
phases.description: The engineering base the official roadmap assumes you already have: Python you can write without copying, plus Git, the shell, HTTP, SQL, testing and logging.

topics.title: The Complete Map of AI Engineering
topics.summary: How AI, ML, deep learning, generative AI, LLMs, RAG and agents fit together, and what an AI engineer actually does.
learning_objectives: Explain how AI, ML, deep learning, generative AI, LLMs, RAG and agents relate to each other
Trace one user request through an AI application from input to output
Decide when an application does not need RAG or agents
Describe what an AI engineer does differently from an ML engineer

topics.title: How Python Runs Your Code, and Core Types
topics.summary: What the interpreter does with a .py file, and how int, float, str, bool and None behave.
learning_objectives: Describe what happens between typing 'python file.py' and seeing output
Predict the type and value of simple expressions without running them
Explain mutability and why it causes surprising bugs

topics.title: Strings, Formatting and Text Handling
topics.summary: Slicing, methods, f-strings and encoding, which is the raw material of every prompt you will ever build.
learning_objectives: Build a multi-line prompt string with f-strings without breaking indentation
Use the string methods that matter for cleaning text
Explain the difference between a str and bytes

topics.title: Lists, Tuples and Iteration
topics.summary: Ordered collections, indexing, slicing and the for loop, plus when a tuple is the honest choice.
learning_objectives: Choose between a list and a tuple and justify it
Slice and iterate without off-by-one errors
Explain what makes a Python object iterable

topics.title: Dictionaries and Sets
topics.summary: Key-value lookup, membership testing and why both are fast, which underpins every JSON payload you will handle.
learning_objectives: Model a record as a dict and access it safely when keys may be missing
Use a set to deduplicate and to test membership
Explain why dict and set lookups do not get slower as they grow

topics.title: Comprehensions and Generators
topics.summary: Expressing a transformation as one readable line, and streaming results instead of building huge lists in memory.
learning_objectives: Rewrite a loop as a comprehension and say when not to
Explain laziness and why a generator can process a file larger than RAM
Predict the memory behaviour of a comprehension versus a generator expression

topics.title: Functions, Arguments and Scope
topics.summary: Parameters, defaults, star-args, return values, and the scope rules that cause mysterious bugs.
learning_objectives: Write a function with a clear contract and no hidden side effects
Explain the mutable default argument trap and avoid it
Describe how Python resolves a name at runtime

topics.title: Errors, Exceptions and Failing Loudly
topics.summary: Reading tracebacks, raising deliberately, catching narrowly, and why a bare except hides the bug you need.
learning_objectives: Read a traceback from the bottom up and locate the real cause
Choose between raising, catching and letting an exception propagate
Explain why catching every exception and passing is almost always wrong

topics.title: Files, JSON and CSV
topics.summary: Reading and writing text safely with context managers, and the two data formats you will meet constantly.
learning_objectives: Read and write files using a with-block and explain what it guarantees
Round-trip a Python object through JSON and name what JSON cannot represent
Parse a CSV with embedded commas and quotes correctly

topics.title: Modules, Packages and Virtual Environments
topics.summary: How imports resolve, what a package is, and why every project gets its own isolated environment.
learning_objectives: Explain how Python finds a module and why the current directory is risky
Create and activate a virtual environment on Windows PowerShell
Split a script into importable modules without circular imports

topics.title: Classes, Objects and Dataclasses
topics.summary: Bundling state with behaviour, and using dataclasses to describe data without ceremony.
learning_objectives: Write a class with a clear responsibility and explain the self parameter
Choose between a dict, a dataclass and a full class
Explain what the initialiser does and does not do

topics.title: Inheritance, Composition and Protocols
topics.summary: Reusing behaviour without creating a fragile hierarchy, and typing against capability instead of class.
learning_objectives: Explain why composition is usually preferable to inheritance
Define a Protocol and explain structural typing
Refactor an inheritance chain into composition

topics.title: Type Hints and Readable Code
topics.summary: Annotations as documentation that tools can check, plus naming and structure that survive your own future reading.
learning_objectives: Annotate functions including optional and container types
Explain that type hints are not enforced at runtime
Name the readability habits that reduce debugging time

topics.title: Git Fundamentals
topics.summary: The object model, staging, committing and reading history, which is how all later work gets recorded.
learning_objectives: Explain the working tree, index and commit as three distinct places
Inspect and interpret status, diff and log output
Write a commit message that explains why, not what

topics.title: GitHub, Branches and Pull Requests
topics.summary: Branching, remotes and the review workflow that makes your portfolio legible to an employer.
learning_objectives: Create a branch, push it and open a pull request
Explain what a merge conflict is and resolve a simple one
Describe what a reviewer looks for in a diff

topics.title: Shell, Paths and Permissions
topics.summary: Navigating, inspecting and piping on both PowerShell and a POSIX shell, including absolute versus relative paths.
learning_objectives: Navigate and inspect a filesystem from the command line
Explain absolute versus relative paths and why scripts break on them
Redirect and pipe command output

topics.title: Processes, Environment Variables and Secret Hygiene
topics.summary: How a process gets its configuration, and why API keys belong in the environment and never in code or Git.
learning_objectives: Set and read an environment variable on Windows and on Unix
Load configuration from the environment with a safe default
Explain concretely what goes wrong when a key is committed

topics.title: HTTP, REST, JSON and Status Codes
topics.summary: Requests, responses, methods, headers, status codes and authentication, which is the shape of every model API.
learning_objectives: Describe the parts of an HTTP request and response
Interpret 2xx, 4xx and 5xx and say who is at fault
Explain how bearer token authentication works

topics.title: Calling APIs from Python: Auth, Retries, Timeouts
topics.summary: Making a real request, handling failure, and the retry and timeout discipline every LLM call needs.
learning_objectives: Call a public API and parse the JSON response
Set a timeout and explain what happens without one
Implement a retry with backoff and say which errors must not be retried

topics.title: SQL Fundamentals: Tables, Queries, Filtering
topics.summary: Relational thinking, SELECT, WHERE and ORDER BY against a local SQLite database.
learning_objectives: Model entities as tables with appropriate keys
Write filtered, sorted queries and read the result honestly
Explain why the database, not Python, should do the filtering

topics.title: Joins, Aggregation and Transactions
topics.summary: Combining tables, grouping, and the atomicity guarantee that matters when an agent writes to a database.
learning_objectives: Write inner and left joins and predict their row counts
Aggregate with GROUP BY and HAVING
Explain a transaction and why an agent action needs one

topics.title: pytest and Writing Tests That Mean Something
topics.summary: Arranging, acting and asserting, testing behaviour instead of implementation, and covering edge cases.
learning_objectives: Write a pytest test for a pure function including edge cases
Assert that an expected exception is raised
Explain why a test that only checks a file exists proves nothing

topics.title: Debugging Systematically
topics.summary: Forming a hypothesis, bisecting, inspecting state and using a debugger instead of guessing.
learning_objectives: Turn a bug report into a falsifiable hypothesis
Reduce a failure to a minimal reproduction
Inspect live state with a breakpoint rather than scattered prints

topics.title: Logging Instead of Printing
topics.summary: Levels, structure and context, which is the first half of the observability you will need in production.
learning_objectives: Configure logging with levels and explain when to use each
Log structured context instead of interpolated prose
Explain why printing does not survive production

topics.title: Dependency Management and Reproducible Environments
topics.summary: Pinning, lockfiles and why works-on-my-machine is a reproducibility failure, not bad luck.
learning_objectives: Pin dependencies so an environment can be rebuilt exactly
Explain the difference between a direct and a transitive dependency
Describe what makes a result reproducible for someone else

phases.title: Mathematics and Machine Learning Fundamentals
phases.description: Not on the official roadmap, and deliberately scoped to intuition plus the few calculations you will actually use. Cosine similarity here is what makes embeddings make sense later.

topics.title: AI, Machine Learning, Deep Learning and Generative AI
topics.summary: Four nested terms people use interchangeably, separated precisely, plus where AGI claims sit.
learning_objectives: Draw the nesting of AI, ML, deep learning and generative AI and place examples in it
Explain what distinguishes a learned system from a rule-based one
Say what current systems do not do, without overclaiming or dismissing

topics.title: Vectors and Matrices
topics.summary: Numbers arranged in a shape, and the operations on them, which is the only representation a model has.
learning_objectives: Read a shape such as (batch, tokens, dimensions) and say what each axis means
Add, scale and multiply vectors and matrices by hand on small examples
Explain why a shape mismatch is the most common deep learning error

topics.title: Dot Products, Norms and Cosine Similarity
topics.summary: The one calculation behind every semantic search, computed by hand before any library does it for you.
learning_objectives: Compute a dot product, a norm and a cosine similarity by hand
Explain why cosine ignores magnitude and when that matters
Predict which of three vectors is most similar to a query vector

topics.title: Probability, Events and Distributions
topics.summary: What a probability is, what a distribution describes, and why a model outputs one over tokens.
learning_objectives: Distinguish a probability, a likelihood and a frequency
Describe a distribution by its shape rather than a single number
Explain what it means for a model to output a distribution over tokens

topics.title: Conditional Probability and Bayes' Theorem
topics.summary: Updating a belief when evidence arrives, which is the mental model for retrieval improving an answer.
learning_objectives: Compute a conditional probability from a small table
Apply Bayes' theorem to a diagnostic example and interpret the result
Explain base rate neglect with a concrete case

topics.title: Descriptive Statistics and Sampling
topics.summary: Means, medians, spread and what a sample can and cannot tell you about a population.
learning_objectives: Choose between mean and median and justify it from the distribution
Explain variance and standard deviation in plain words
Say what a sample of 20 evaluation cases can and cannot establish

topics.title: Correlation, Causation and Confounding
topics.summary: Why a metric moving together with another proves very little, which is the core evaluation trap.
learning_objectives: Compute and interpret a correlation coefficient
Identify a plausible confounder in a stated claim
Rewrite an overclaiming result statement into an honest one

topics.title: Supervised, Unsupervised and Reinforcement Learning
topics.summary: The three ways a system can be given a learning signal, and which one an LLM is trained with.
learning_objectives: Classify a problem into the right paradigm and justify it
Explain what a label is and what it costs to obtain
Describe where reinforcement learning from feedback fits in LLM training

topics.title: Regression: Predicting a Number
topics.summary: Fitting a line, reading coefficients and understanding residuals, with scikit-learn as the tool not the lesson.
learning_objectives: Fit and interpret a linear regression on a small dataset
Read a residual plot and say what it reveals
Explain why a good fit on training data proves nothing

topics.title: Classification: Predicting a Category
topics.summary: Decision boundaries, probabilities and thresholds, and why the threshold is a product decision.
learning_objectives: Train a classifier and inspect its predicted probabilities
Explain what moving the decision threshold trades away
Describe a decision boundary in two dimensions

topics.title: Clustering: Finding Structure Without Labels
topics.summary: Grouping by similarity, which is exactly what you will later do to embeddings.
learning_objectives: Run k-means and interpret the clusters critically
Explain how the distance metric changes the result
Say why cluster quality is hard to evaluate without labels

topics.title: Dimensionality Reduction
topics.summary: Compressing many dimensions to few, how it helps visualisation, and how it misleads.
learning_objectives: Reduce a dataset to two dimensions and plot it
Explain what information is lost and why
Describe why distances in a reduced plot cannot be trusted literally

topics.title: Features, Labels and Preprocessing
topics.summary: Turning raw data into model input: scaling, encoding, missing values and the judgement each requires.
learning_objectives: Encode categorical and numeric features appropriately
Handle missing values with a stated, defensible policy
Explain why scaling matters for distance-based methods

topics.title: Train, Validation and Test Splits
topics.summary: Three datasets with three different jobs, and the discipline that keeps a result honest.
learning_objectives: Explain the distinct purpose of each split
Describe what happens when the test set is used for tuning
Split time-ordered data correctly

topics.title: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1 and ROC-AUC
topics.summary: What each metric rewards, and why accuracy is the wrong default for imbalanced problems.
learning_objectives: Compute precision, recall and F1 from a confusion matrix by hand
Choose the right metric for a stated business cost
Explain what ROC-AUC measures and what it hides

topics.title: Regression Metrics
topics.summary: MAE, MSE, RMSE and R-squared, what each punishes, and which to report.
learning_objectives: Compute MAE and RMSE on a small example
Explain why RMSE punishes large errors more
Interpret R-squared without overreading it

topics.title: Overfitting, Underfitting, Regularization and Cross-Validation
topics.summary: Memorising versus generalising, and the techniques that detect and reduce the gap.
learning_objectives: Diagnose overfitting from training and validation curves
Explain how regularization constrains a model
Run k-fold cross-validation and interpret the spread, not just the mean

topics.title: Data Leakage, Class Imbalance and Baselines
topics.summary: The three ways results get silently invalidated, and the baseline that keeps you honest.
learning_objectives: Identify leakage in a described pipeline
Handle class imbalance and report it honestly
Build a trivial baseline and compare any model against it first

phases.title: Deep Learning Essentials
phases.description: Scoped to the depth needed to read a model card and explain a transformer, not to train models from scratch. Attention here is what makes context windows and embeddings stop being magic.

topics.title: Neurons, Weights and Biases
topics.summary: The single unit of computation, built by hand in NumPy before any framework appears.
learning_objectives: Compute a single neuron's output by hand
Explain what a weight and a bias each control
Describe a layer as a matrix multiplication

topics.title: Activation Functions
topics.summary: Why a network without non-linearity is just a line, and what ReLU, sigmoid and softmax each do.
learning_objectives: Explain why non-linearity is necessary
Choose an activation for a hidden layer and for an output layer
Describe what softmax produces and why it suits token prediction

topics.title: Loss Functions
topics.summary: How wrongness is turned into a single number the model can minimise.
learning_objectives: Compute cross-entropy loss on a small example
Explain why the loss, not the metric, is what training optimises
Say what a loss of zero on training data would actually mean

topics.title: Forward Propagation
topics.summary: Walking an input through the network to a prediction, traced by hand through a tiny network.
learning_objectives: Trace an input through a two-layer network by hand
Track tensor shapes at every step
Explain where the parameters live

topics.title: Backpropagation
topics.summary: How the error is attributed back to each parameter, explained as repeated use of the chain rule.
learning_objectives: Explain backpropagation as blame assignment in plain words
Compute a gradient for a single weight by hand
Describe why vanishing gradients happen

topics.title: Gradient Descent and Learning Rates
topics.summary: Taking small steps downhill, and why the step size decides whether training works at all.
learning_objectives: Explain gradient descent with the hill analogy and then without it
Predict what happens with a learning rate that is too high or too low
Describe what an optimiser such as Adam adds

topics.title: PyTorch Tensors
topics.summary: The array type with gradients attached, plus devices, dtypes and the shape discipline.
learning_objectives: Create, reshape and broadcast tensors deliberately
Explain what requires_grad changes
Move a tensor between devices and explain the cost

topics.title: Datasets and DataLoaders
topics.summary: Feeding data in batches, and why batching changes both speed and gradients.
learning_objectives: Write a Dataset and iterate it with a DataLoader
Explain what batch size trades off
Say why shuffling matters

topics.title: A Training Loop End to End
topics.summary: The five lines that are the whole of training, written once by hand so frameworks stop being opaque.
learning_objectives: Write a training loop from scratch and explain each step
Explain why gradients must be zeroed
Diagnose a loss that does not decrease

topics.title: Validation, Inference and Eval Mode
topics.summary: Separating learning from predicting, and the switches that must be flipped for each.
learning_objectives: Explain what eval mode and no-grad change
Detect overfitting from a validation curve
Describe the difference between training cost and inference cost

topics.title: Embeddings and Representation Learning
topics.summary: How a model turns discrete things into positions in space, and why nearness there means similarity.
learning_objectives: Explain an embedding as a learned lookup table
Describe what makes two embeddings close
Say why embeddings from different models cannot be compared

topics.title: The Attention Mechanism
topics.summary: Queries, keys and values, worked through on a short sentence by hand.
learning_objectives: Explain query, key and value in your own words
Compute attention weights for a three-token example
Explain why attention cost grows quadratically with sequence length

topics.title: Transformer Architecture
topics.summary: Stacking attention and feed-forward blocks, positional information, and what the stack produces.
learning_objectives: Describe the components of a transformer block and their order
Explain why positional information must be added explicitly
Trace a token from input to output logits

topics.title: GPU and Memory Basics
topics.summary: Why accelerators matter, where memory goes, and how to estimate whether a model fits.
learning_objectives: Estimate the memory a model's weights require at a given precision
Explain why a GPU suits matrix multiplication
Describe what runs out first when a model will not load

phases.title: LLMs, Model Platforms and Prompt Engineering
phases.description: The official roadmap's core: how LLMs behave, which model to pick, how to call it, and how to shape a prompt. Ends by building the small evaluation harness reused by every later phase.

topics.title: How LLMs Work
topics.summary: Next-token prediction, why that single mechanism produces apparent reasoning, and what it cannot guarantee.
learning_objectives: Explain next-token prediction and why it yields fluent text
Say what the model is and is not doing when it appears to reason
Explain why the same prompt can give different answers

topics.title: Tokens and Tokenization
topics.summary: The units a model actually sees, why they are not words, and why they are what you pay for.
learning_objectives: Tokenize text and explain the token count you get
Explain why token boundaries break character-level tasks
Estimate the cost of a request from its token counts

topics.title: Context and the Context Window
topics.summary: The finite working memory of a request, what fills it, and what happens at the limit.
learning_objectives: Explain what occupies the context window in a real request
Describe what happens when the window is exceeded
Explain why a larger window is not automatically better

topics.title: Pretraining, Fine-Tuning and Inference
topics.summary: The three distinct lifecycle stages, who pays for each, and which one you actually operate.
learning_objectives: Separate the three stages by purpose, cost and who performs them
Explain what a model's knowledge cutoff means in practice
Say which stage you can change and which you cannot

topics.title: Sampling and Temperature
topics.summary: How a distribution over tokens becomes one chosen token, and what temperature really changes.
learning_objectives: Explain how a token is selected from a probability distribution
Predict the effect of temperature 0 versus 1 on a given task
Choose a temperature for extraction and for brainstorming, and justify both

topics.title: Top-K, Top-P and Repetition Penalties
topics.summary: The remaining generation controls, what each truncates or discourages, and when to touch them at all.
learning_objectives: Explain top-k and top-p and how they interact with temperature
Describe what a repetition penalty fixes and what it breaks
Decide which parameters to leave at their defaults

topics.title: Types of Models: Pre-trained, Closed, Open and Self-Hosted
topics.summary: The deployment and licensing axes that decide what you are allowed and able to do.
learning_objectives: Distinguish closed, open-weight and self-hosted and name a trade-off for each
Explain what a pre-trained model gives you for free
Say what a licence can restrict even for downloadable weights

topics.title: Closed Model Families
topics.summary: The hosted frontier families, how their capability tiers are organised, and how to read a model card.
learning_objectives: Read a model card and extract context length, modality and pricing
Explain what a capability tier within a family usually trades
Describe how to track a provider's deprecations

topics.title: Open-Weight Model Families
topics.summary: The downloadable families, their size classes, and what each size class realistically runs on.
learning_objectives: Match a model size class to the hardware it needs
Explain what open weights allow that a hosted API does not
Say where open-weight models still lag and where they do not

topics.title: Hugging Face Hub and Tasks
topics.summary: The registry for models, datasets and task definitions, and how to navigate it without drowning.
learning_objectives: Find a model for a stated task and check its licence and size
Explain what a task definition standardises
Load a small model and run one inference locally

topics.title: Local Inference with Ollama and LM Studio
topics.summary: Running a model on your own machine, and the latency, cost and privacy picture that changes.
learning_objectives: Run a local model and measure its latency
Explain when local inference is the right choice and when it is not
Describe what quantization did to the model you downloaded

topics.title: Hosted Model APIs
topics.summary: The request and response shape shared across providers, and the SDK versus raw HTTP decision.
learning_objectives: Call a hosted model API and parse the response
Explain the common message and role structure
Handle rate limits, timeouts and partial failures

topics.title: OpenAI-Compatible APIs and Routing
topics.summary: Why one request shape became a de facto standard, and how routing across providers works.
learning_objectives: Point the same client at two different providers
Explain what a compatible API does and does not guarantee
Describe a reason to route rather than hardcode one model

topics.title: Choosing the Right Model
topics.summary: A defensible selection method using capability, latency, cost and constraints instead of reputation.
learning_objectives: Build a selection matrix for a stated task and defend the choice
Compute cost per thousand requests from token estimates
Explain why the best benchmark score is often the wrong pick

topics.title: Prompt Anatomy: Instructions, Role, Context and Constraints
topics.summary: The parts of a prompt and what each part is responsible for, tested by changing one part at a time.
learning_objectives: Separate a prompt into system instruction, role, context and constraints
Explain what a system instruction can and cannot enforce
Improve a weak prompt by changing exactly one element

topics.title: Zero-Shot, Few-Shot, Chain-of-Thought and ReAct
topics.summary: The four patterns worth knowing, what each costs in tokens, and when each stops helping.
learning_objectives: Apply each of the four patterns to the same task and compare results
Explain why few-shot examples can bias the output
Say when chain-of-thought is not worth the tokens

topics.title: Structured Output and Schema Validation
topics.summary: Getting parseable data out of a text model, and validating it instead of trusting it.
learning_objectives: Request and validate JSON output against a schema
Handle the case where the model returns invalid structure
Explain why validation is required even with a schema-constrained mode

topics.title: Function Calling Fundamentals
topics.summary: Letting the model request a function call, and why your code, not the model, decides what runs.
learning_objectives: Define a tool schema and handle a tool call request end to end
Explain that the model proposes and your code disposes
Describe what happens when the model invents an argument

topics.title: Prompt Caching
topics.summary: Reusing a stable prefix to cut cost and latency, and the ordering discipline it forces on prompts.
learning_objectives: Structure a prompt so a cache can hit
Measure the cost and latency difference a cache hit makes
Explain what invalidates a cached prefix

topics.title: Streaming Responses
topics.summary: Delivering tokens as they are produced, and what that changes for your code and your user.
learning_objectives: Consume a streamed response and render it incrementally
Explain why streaming improves perceived latency but not total latency
Handle an error that arrives mid-stream

topics.title: Hallucinations, Grounding and Limits
topics.summary: Why a fluent wrong answer is the default failure mode, and what grounding does and does not fix.
learning_objectives: Explain why hallucination is intrinsic to next-token prediction
Distinguish a knowledge gap from a reasoning failure from a prompt failure
Say what grounding fixes and what it leaves untouched

topics.title: Inference Engineering Overview
topics.summary: Where latency and cost actually come from at serving time, as a map for the optimisation phase later.
learning_objectives: Separate time to first token from tokens per second and say what each depends on
Explain why batching helps throughput but can hurt latency
Name the levers available to you versus only to the provider

topics.title: Build a Minimal Evaluation Harness
topics.summary: A small, dependency-free runner over a fixed case file, used to measure every change from here on.
learning_objectives: Build a harness that runs fixed cases and reports pass rate, latency and cost
Write cases that would actually fail if the system regressed
Explain why a result without a baseline is not evidence

phases.title: Context Engineering
phases.description: A first-class section on the official 2026 roadmap and the largest gap in the original plan. This is the vocabulary for things already built by instinct in DocMind and the payment agent.

topics.title: Context Engineering versus Prompt Engineering
topics.summary: Writing instructions versus deciding what information reaches the model at all, and why the second dominates.
learning_objectives: State the difference in one sentence and defend it with an example
Identify which of two failing systems has a context problem
Explain why a better prompt cannot fix missing information

topics.title: What Is a Context Layer
topics.summary: The component that assembles the final request from many sources, treated as real software with a contract.
learning_objectives: Describe the responsibilities of a context layer
Draw the assembly path from sources to final request
Explain why assembly logic belongs in testable code

topics.title: Context Sources
topics.summary: User input, history, retrieved documents, tool results, profiles and system state, each with different trust.
learning_objectives: Enumerate the sources feeding one real request
Assign a trust level to each source and justify it
Explain why source order inside the prompt changes behaviour

topics.title: State and Historical Context
topics.summary: Carrying a conversation forward without carrying everything, and where turn state actually lives.
learning_objectives: Explain why a model has no memory between requests
Design what to carry forward across turns and what to drop
Describe the cost growth of naive history accumulation

topics.title: Memory Systems
topics.summary: Short-term, long-term and episodic memory as engineering choices, with explicit write and read rules.
learning_objectives: Distinguish short-term, long-term and episodic memory by lifetime and use
Define when a fact is promoted to long-term memory
Explain how a wrong memory becomes a permanent bug

topics.title: Context Compaction
topics.summary: Summarising, pruning and dropping to fit the window, and what each technique loses.
learning_objectives: Implement a compaction strategy and measure what it loses
Explain the risk of summarising a summary
Choose what must never be compacted

topics.title: Long-Context Processing
topics.summary: What actually happens as the window grows, including position effects and attention dilution.
learning_objectives: Describe the lost-in-the-middle effect and test for it
Explain why relevant information should be placed deliberately
Compare a long window against retrieval on cost and accuracy

topics.title: RAG and Dynamic Filters as Context Strategy
topics.summary: Retrieval framed as a context decision, with filters narrowing what is even eligible to be retrieved.
learning_objectives: Explain retrieval as dynamic context selection
Apply a metadata filter before similarity search and say why order matters
Describe a case where a filter silently removes the right answer

topics.title: Context Isolation and Multi-Agent Sharing
topics.summary: Keeping contexts separate on purpose, and the rules for passing information between agents.
learning_objectives: Explain why isolating contexts can improve reliability
Define what one agent may pass to another
Describe how an error propagates through shared context

topics.title: Context Security
topics.summary: Untrusted content inside the context window, instruction and data confusion, and tenant separation.
learning_objectives: Explain why retrieved text must never be treated as instructions
Separate instruction channels from data channels in a prompt
Describe a concrete cross-tenant leak and how to prevent it

topics.title: Context Evaluation
topics.summary: Measuring whether the right information arrived, separately from whether the answer was good.
learning_objectives: Measure context precision and context recall on a small set
Attribute a bad answer to retrieval, assembly or generation
Explain why answer quality alone cannot diagnose a context bug

topics.title: Context Failure Modes
topics.summary: The named ways context breaks: poisoning, distraction, confusion, clash and staleness.
learning_objectives: Name the common context failure modes and give an example of each
Diagnose which mode a given bad output exhibits
Propose a detection signal for one of them

topics.title: Context Tooling and Data Catalogues
topics.summary: Where enterprise context actually lives, and what a catalogue or product analytics store contributes.
learning_objectives: Explain what a data catalogue adds to a context layer
Describe how product event data becomes useful context
Say why metadata governance becomes an AI problem

phases.title: Embeddings and Vector Databases
phases.description: Semantic representation and retrieval, measured rather than assumed. The cosine similarity from Phase 2 becomes the thing you depend on daily.

topics.title: What Are Embeddings
topics.summary: Turning text into a position in space so that nearness means relatedness, with purpose and limits.
learning_objectives: Explain an embedding without using the word vector
Compute the similarity between three short texts and interpret the ranking
Explain why embeddings from two different models are incomparable

topics.title: Embedding Models and How to Choose One
topics.summary: Hosted and local embedding models, dimensionality, max input length, and the cost of switching.
learning_objectives: Compare two embedding models on the same retrieval set
Explain what dimensionality trades off
Describe what must be rebuilt when you change embedding model

topics.title: Chunking and Document Preprocessing
topics.summary: Splitting documents so that a retrieved piece is both findable and sufficient on its own.
learning_objectives: Implement fixed, overlapping and structure-aware chunking
Explain how chunk size changes both recall and answer quality
Identify a document type where naive chunking destroys meaning

topics.title: Indexing Embeddings
topics.summary: Storing vectors so they can be searched, and what an index actually builds.
learning_objectives: Build an index over a document set and report its size
Explain what is stored besides the vector
Describe the cost of reindexing

topics.title: Similarity Search and Distance Metrics
topics.summary: Exact search first, then the metrics, so that approximation is understood as a deliberate trade.
learning_objectives: Implement exact nearest-neighbour search by hand
Compare cosine, dot product and Euclidean on the same data
Explain what top-k actually returns

topics.title: Approximate Nearest Neighbour Search
topics.summary: Why exact search stops scaling, and what HNSW and IVF trade away to be fast.
learning_objectives: Explain the recall versus latency trade in approximate search
Describe at a high level how a graph index finds neighbours
Measure the recall loss of an approximate index against exact search

topics.title: Vector Databases
topics.summary: What a vector database adds beyond a library, and how the common options differ in practice.
learning_objectives: Store and query vectors in a local vector database
Explain what persistence, filtering and multi-tenancy add
Justify choosing a library over a database for a small corpus

topics.title: Metadata Filtering
topics.summary: Narrowing the candidate set by attributes, and the subtle interaction between filter and similarity.
learning_objectives: Combine a metadata filter with similarity search
Explain pre-filtering versus post-filtering and their different failure modes
Show how a filter can silently exclude the correct chunk

topics.title: Semantic Search
topics.summary: The end-to-end search experience, and where semantic search beats and loses to keyword search.
learning_objectives: Build a working semantic search over a document set
Name three queries where keyword search wins
Explain why semantic search returns confident nonsense for out-of-corpus queries

topics.title: Sparse and Dense Retrieval
topics.summary: Keyword scoring such as BM25 against embedding similarity, each understood on its own first.
learning_objectives: Implement or run BM25 and compare it against dense retrieval
Explain what a sparse representation captures that a dense one loses
Choose the right method for an exact-identifier lookup

topics.title: Hybrid Retrieval and Score Fusion
topics.summary: Combining sparse and dense results honestly, including why raw scores cannot simply be added.
learning_objectives: Fuse two ranked lists with reciprocal rank fusion
Explain why score normalisation is required for weighted fusion
Measure whether hybrid actually beat both components

topics.title: Reranking and Relevance Scoring
topics.summary: A second, more expensive pass over a shortlist, and the latency it costs.
learning_objectives: Add a reranker over the top-k shortlist and measure the gain
Explain why a cross-encoder is more accurate and slower
Decide a shortlist size from a latency budget

topics.title: Retrieval Evaluation: Recall@k, MRR and nDCG
topics.summary: Measuring retrieval separately from generation, using a labelled set you build yourself.
learning_objectives: Build a small labelled retrieval set and compute Recall@k and MRR
Explain what nDCG adds over Recall@k
State what a retrieval metric does not prove about answer quality

topics.title: Other Uses of Embeddings
topics.summary: Classification, deduplication, recommendation and anomaly detection, often without an LLM at all.
learning_objectives: Classify texts using embeddings and a nearest-centroid rule
Detect near-duplicates in a document set
Explain when embeddings alone beat calling an LLM

phases.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
phases.description: The full RAG pipeline, built, measured, broken and repaired. This phase upgrades DocMind against a baseline you measure first.

topics.title: What Is RAG, and When Not to Use It
topics.summary: Retrieval plus generation as one system, the problems it solves, and the cheaper options to rule out first.
learning_objectives: Explain RAG as a pipeline with named stages
Name two problems RAG does not solve
Identify a case where a database query beats RAG

topics.title: RAG versus Fine-Tuning versus Prompting
topics.summary: Matching the technique to the problem: missing knowledge, wrong behaviour, or wrong format.
learning_objectives: Choose between prompting, RAG and fine-tuning for three stated problems
Explain why fine-tuning is a poor way to add facts
Describe a system that needs both RAG and fine-tuning

topics.title: Document Ingestion and Extraction
topics.summary: Getting text out of PDFs, HTML and scans, where most real RAG quality is won or lost.
learning_objectives: Extract text from a messy PDF and inspect what was lost
Explain why table and layout structure breaks naive extraction
Build an ingestion report that surfaces extraction failures

topics.title: Cleaning and Chunking Experiments
topics.summary: Running chunking as a measured experiment rather than a guess, using the retrieval metrics from Phase 6.
learning_objectives: Run three chunking strategies and compare Recall@k
Explain which document properties drove the winner
Record the experiment so someone else can reproduce it

topics.title: The Embedding and Indexing Pipeline
topics.summary: Batching, idempotency, incremental updates and the cost of a full rebuild.
learning_objectives: Build an idempotent ingestion pipeline that can resume
Handle a document that changed without duplicating it
Report the time and cost of indexing your corpus

topics.title: The Retrieval Process
topics.summary: Query to candidates to shortlist, with every parameter made explicit and logged.
learning_objectives: Implement retrieval with filters, hybrid search and reranking
Log every retrieval decision for later diagnosis
Explain each parameter's effect on the result set

topics.title: Query Processing and Rewriting
topics.summary: Fixing the question before searching: expansion, decomposition and the risks of each.
learning_objectives: Implement query rewriting and measure whether it helped
Decompose a multi-part question into sub-queries
Show a case where rewriting made retrieval worse

topics.title: Context Assembly
topics.summary: Turning retrieved chunks into a prompt: ordering, deduplication, budgeting and truncation.
learning_objectives: Assemble a prompt within a fixed token budget
Explain how chunk ordering changes the answer
Handle the case where retrieved content exceeds the budget

topics.title: Grounded Generation
topics.summary: Instructing the model to answer only from context, and verifying that it did.
learning_objectives: Write a grounding instruction and test it with an unanswerable question
Make the system say it does not know, reliably
Explain why grounding instructions are not a guarantee

topics.title: Citations and Source Verification
topics.summary: Attributing each claim to a retrieved span, and checking the attribution programmatically.
learning_objectives: Produce answers with per-claim citations
Verify automatically that a cited span supports the claim
Report a citation correctness rate for your own system

topics.title: Prompt Injection Through Retrieved Documents
topics.summary: What happens when a document in your corpus contains instructions, and how to keep it data.
learning_objectives: Demonstrate an injection through a planted document in a local corpus
Separate instruction and data channels so the injection fails
Explain why output filtering alone is insufficient

topics.title: Access Control and Document Permissions
topics.summary: Making retrieval respect who is asking, enforced at the data layer rather than in the prompt.
learning_objectives: Enforce per-user document permissions during retrieval
Explain why a prompt instruction is not an access control mechanism
Write a test that fails if a user can retrieve a forbidden document

topics.title: RAG Answer Evaluation
topics.summary: Faithfulness, answer relevance and citation correctness, measured on a set you built.
learning_objectives: Build a RAG evaluation set with expected sources
Measure faithfulness and answer relevance and report both
Explain what each metric fails to capture

topics.title: RAG Error Analysis
topics.summary: Separating retrieval failure from assembly failure from generation failure, case by case.
learning_objectives: Classify twenty failures by failing stage
Fix the single highest-frequency cause and re-measure
Explain why fixing the prompt first is usually the wrong move

topics.title: Implementation Choices: SDKs Directly or a Framework
topics.summary: What LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack and RAGFlow give you, and what they take away.
learning_objectives: Rebuild one pipeline stage with a framework and compare the code
Name what a framework hides that you now know you need to see
Decide, with reasons, what DocMind should use

topics.title: Project: Upgrade DocMind
topics.summary: Baseline, then targeted improvements, then a metrics-first write-up with reproducible commands.
learning_objectives: Measure and record a baseline before changing anything
Improve one measured metric and show the before and after
Write a README that states what was measured and what it does not prove

phases.title: AI Agents, Tools and MCP
phases.description: Deterministic workflows first, bounded autonomy second. Includes MCP in depth, and the safety work pulled forward from the official safety section because this phase touches payment data.

topics.title: LLM Application, Workflow or Agent
topics.summary: Three designs with very different reliability, cost and debuggability, and how to pick the least powerful one that works.
learning_objectives: Classify three described systems correctly and justify each
Explain why a workflow is usually more reliable than an agent
State the condition that genuinely requires an agent

topics.title: Agent Use Cases and Non-Use-Cases
topics.summary: Where agents pay off, where they are a liability, and how to recognise each in advance.
learning_objectives: Name three tasks suited to agents and three that are not
Explain why open-ended tasks degrade agent reliability
Reframe one agent idea as a deterministic workflow

topics.title: Tools and Function Execution
topics.summary: Designing a tool interface a model can use correctly, and validating every argument it sends.
learning_objectives: Design a tool schema with unambiguous names and descriptions
Validate and reject malformed tool arguments
Explain why a tool must be safe when called with wrong arguments

topics.title: ReAct Prompting
topics.summary: Interleaving reasoning and action, written manually before any framework provides it.
learning_objectives: Implement a ReAct loop by hand
Explain what the reasoning step contributes and what it does not guarantee
Identify a loop that is reasoning without making progress

topics.title: The Agent Loop, Planning and Termination
topics.summary: Observe, decide, act, repeat, plus the termination conditions that stop it running forever.
learning_objectives: Implement an agent loop with explicit step and time limits
Detect a non-progressing loop and halt it
Explain why termination conditions are a safety feature

topics.title: Agent State and Memory
topics.summary: What the agent knows between steps, where it is stored, and how it is kept consistent.
learning_objectives: Separate durable state from per-step scratch context
Persist state so a crashed run can resume
Explain how stale state produces a wrong action

topics.title: Workflow Orchestration and State Graphs
topics.summary: Modelling a process as explicit nodes and transitions, with LangGraph as one implementation.
learning_objectives: Model a multi-step process as a state graph
Explain why an explicit graph is easier to test than a free-running loop
Add a conditional branch and a retry edge

topics.title: Single-Agent and Multi-Agent Architectures
topics.summary: When splitting into several agents helps, and the coordination cost it introduces.
learning_objectives: Compare a single agent against a supervisor pattern for one task
Explain how errors compound across agents
Decide, with reasons, against multi-agent for a given problem

topics.title: Tool Permissions and Human Approval
topics.summary: Least privilege for tools, and the approval gate in front of anything consequential.
learning_objectives: Classify tools as read-only, reversible or consequential
Implement an approval gate that blocks until a human decides
Explain why the model must never hold the authority to approve

topics.title: Retries, Timeouts and Idempotency
topics.summary: Making a retried action safe, which is the difference between a demo and a system touching money.
learning_objectives: Make a side-effecting tool idempotent with a request key
Explain what a retry without idempotency does to a payment
Set timeouts at every external boundary

topics.title: Failure Recovery and Compensation
topics.summary: What happens after a step fails halfway, and how to leave the system in a defined state.
learning_objectives: Design a compensating action for a failed multi-step operation
Explain why rollback is often impossible and what replaces it
Write a test that injects a mid-run failure

topics.title: Guardrails, Budgets and Action Limits
topics.summary: Hard limits on spend, steps, tool calls and blast radius, enforced in code rather than in prompts.
learning_objectives: Enforce a spend and step budget that halts the run
Explain why a prompt instruction is not a limit
Choose limits from a stated worst-case cost

topics.title: Agent Traces and Observability
topics.summary: Recording every decision so a failure can be explained after the fact.
learning_objectives: Emit a structured trace covering every step, tool call and decision
Reconstruct a failed run from its trace alone
Explain what must be redacted from a trace

topics.title: Building an Agent Without a Framework
topics.summary: The whole loop in plain Python, so that every framework afterwards is legible.
learning_objectives: Build a working tool-using agent with no agent framework
Explain each part a framework would have provided
Identify the parts you would not want to maintain yourself

topics.title: Agent SDKs and Platforms
topics.summary: What the major agent SDKs and platform builders provide, compared against your manual version.
learning_objectives: Rebuild one agent with an SDK and compare lines of code and control
Name what each SDK decides for you
Choose a stack for one project and defend it

topics.title: Model Context Protocol: What and Why
topics.summary: A standard interface between models and tools or data, and the problem it is solving.
learning_objectives: Explain what problem MCP standardises
Compare MCP against hand-written tool integrations
Say when MCP is unnecessary

topics.title: MCP Hosts, Clients and Servers
topics.summary: The three roles, who talks to whom, and where your code sits in each case.
learning_objectives: Name the three roles and their responsibilities
Trace a tool invocation across the roles
Identify which role you are implementing in a given task

topics.title: MCP Data and Transport Layers
topics.summary: The message layer and the connection layer, and why local and remote differ.
learning_objectives: Explain the data layer and the transport layer separately
Compare a local and a remote transport on trust and latency
Describe how capabilities are negotiated

topics.title: Building an MCP Server and Client
topics.summary: Exposing your own tools and resources over MCP, then consuming them.
learning_objectives: Build an MCP server exposing one tool and one resource
Connect to it from a client and invoke the tool
Connect to a remote server and explain the added trust questions

topics.title: Agent Evaluation and Simulation
topics.summary: Scoring an agent on task success, cost and safety violations, using simulated scenarios.
learning_objectives: Build a scenario suite with expected outcomes
Report task success rate, steps, cost and safety violations
Explain why a single successful run is not evidence

topics.title: Deterministic Workflows versus Autonomy
topics.summary: The reliability cost of each unit of autonomy, and how to spend it deliberately.
learning_objectives: Quantify the reliability difference between two designs of one task
Describe how to add autonomy incrementally with measurement
Explain the production argument for the least autonomous design

topics.title: Project: Make the Payment Recovery Agent Reliable
topics.summary: Traces, offline evaluation, idempotency, budgets, approval and simulated failure injection. Mock providers only.
learning_objectives: Establish a baseline recovery rate on simulated cases
Add idempotency, budgets, approval and traces, then re-measure
State clearly which results are simulated and what they do not prove

topics.title: Project: A Bounded Research or Coding Agent
topics.summary: A new agent built workflow-first, with explicit tool permissions, limits, traces and evaluation cases.
learning_objectives: Ship a deterministic version before adding any planning
Enforce tool permissions and execution limits in code
Provide evaluation cases and a trace for every run

phases.title: Multimodal AI
phases.description: Images, audio and speech, ending in a measured upgrade to VINI AI with word error rate, task success and latency numbers rather than impressions.

topics.title: Multimodal AI and Its Use Cases
topics.summary: What changes when a model accepts more than text, and which tasks genuinely need it.
learning_objectives: Explain how non-text input is represented for a model
Name three tasks that need multimodality and two that do not
Describe the cost difference against a text-only request

topics.title: Image Understanding
topics.summary: Sending images to a vision-language model, and what it reliably can and cannot read.
learning_objectives: Send an image and extract structured information from it
Identify a case where the model misreads a chart or table
Explain how image resolution affects tokens and cost

topics.title: Image Generation
topics.summary: Generating and editing images, prompt control, and the evaluation problem it creates.
learning_objectives: Generate an image to a specification and iterate on the prompt
Explain why image quality is hard to evaluate automatically
Describe the provenance and rights questions generation raises

topics.title: Video Understanding
topics.summary: Frames, sampling and the cost of time-based input.
learning_objectives: Sample frames from a clip and reason over them

Say what is lost when video becomes still frames

topics.title: Audio Representations
topics.summary: Waveforms, sample rates and spectrograms, and why audio becomes a picture before a model sees it.
learning_objectives: Explain sample rate and what is lost by lowering it
Describe a spectrogram in plain words
Say why audio preprocessing affects recognition accuracy

topics.title: Speech to Text
topics.summary: Transcription, its failure modes, and measuring it with word error rate.
learning_objectives: Transcribe audio and compute word error rate against a reference
Identify the conditions that degrade recognition most

topics.title: Text to Speech
topics.summary: Synthesising speech, controlling delivery, and the latency budget of a spoken reply.

topics.title: Speech Pipelines and Turn-Taking
topics.summary: Wiring recognition, reasoning and synthesis into a conversation that does not talk over the user.

topics.title: Interruptions, Barge-In and Error Handling
topics.summary: Handling the user cutting in, mishearings and silence, which is most of what makes voice usable.

Recover gracefully from a low-confidence transcription
Explain why a voice system must never silently guess

topics.title: Tool Calling Through a Voice Interface
topics.summary: Confirming consequential actions out loud, and the permission boundary for a spoken command.
learning_objectives: Add a confirmed tool call to a voice loop
Explain why voice raises the bar for confirmation
Describe how a mishearing could trigger a wrong action and prevent it

topics.title: Project: Upgrade VINI AI
topics.summary: Measured improvements to recognition, latency, interruption handling and task success.
learning_objectives: Baseline word error rate, task success rate and end-to-end latency
Improve one of them and show the before and after
State the conditions your measurements do and do not cover

phases.title: Fine-Tuning and Model Optimization
phases.description: The phase the official roadmap deliberately leaves out, kept because the payment agent is self-distilling. Every technique here is gated on measuring that it was needed.

topics.title: Prompting, RAG or Fine-Tuning: Deciding Honestly
topics.summary: A decision procedure that rules out the cheaper options first, with the evidence each requires.
learning_objectives: Apply a decision procedure to three stated problems
State the evidence that would justify fine-tuning
Explain why fine-tuning is the wrong tool for adding facts

topics.title: Dataset Design and Preparation
topics.summary: Where examples come from, how many are needed, and why data quality dominates every other choice.

topics.title: Supervised Fine-Tuning
topics.summary: The actual training run, its hyperparameters, and reading the loss curve honestly.
learning_objectives: Run a small supervised fine-tune and read the loss curves

topics.title: LoRA and QLoRA

topics.title: Quantization

topics.title: GPU Memory and Capacity Planning
topics.summary: Estimating whether a model and its workload fit before renting the hardware.

topics.title: Evaluating Before and After Optimization
topics.summary: The measurement discipline that makes an optimisation claim real rather than hopeful.

topics.title: Latency, Throughput and Cost Trade-offs

topics.title: When Not to Optimize

phases.title: Backend Engineering and Deployment
phases.description: The official roadmap defers this to the Backend roadmap. Kept in full, because an AI feature nobody can call is not a system. AutoBI is hardened here.

topics.title: FastAPI Fundamentals and Application Structure
topics.summary: Routing, dependency injection and a project layout that survives growth.

topics.title: Request Validation and Response Models

topics.title: Rate Limiting and Quotas

topics.title: Structured Logging in Production
topics.summary: Logs you can query, correlated by request, with nothing sensitive in them.
learning_objectives: Emit correlated structured logs across a request
Redact prompts and personal data appropriately
Answer a specific production question using only logs

topics.title: Monitoring, Health Checks and Alerting
topics.summary: Knowing a system is broken before a user reports it, and alerting on symptoms not causes.
learning_objectives: Expose health and readiness endpoints and explain the difference
Define the few metrics worth alerting on
Explain why alerting on CPU is usually wrong

topics.title: Cost Controls and Resource Management
topics.summary: Caps, alerts and attribution, so an AI feature cannot quietly spend without limit.
learning_objectives: Attribute spend per feature and per user
Implement a hard cap with a defined behaviour on breach
Build a cost forecast from measured usage

topics.title: Load and Latency Testing
topics.summary: Finding the breaking point on purpose, and reporting tail latency rather than averages.
learning_objectives: Load test an endpoint and report p50, p95 and p99
Explain why an average latency hides the user experience
Identify the component that saturates first

topics.title: Project: Harden AutoBI
topics.summary: CSV validation, schema inference, profiling, safeguarded SQL generation and output verification, with regression tests.
learning_objectives: Validate and profile arbitrary CSV input without crashing
Generate SQL with safeguards and verify results before display
Explain which parts should not use an LLM at all

phases.title: Evaluation, Observability, Safety and Reliability
phases.description: The official roadmap's safety, observability, evaluation and regression testing sections in full. Parts were pulled forward into Phases 7 and 8; this is where they become rigorous.

topics.title: Deterministic Evaluations
topics.summary: Checks with one correct answer, which should always be tried before an LLM judge.
learning_objectives: Write deterministic checks for format, schema and exact facts
Explain why a deterministic check beats a judged one when available
Convert one subjective criterion into a deterministic one

topics.title: Model-Based Evaluations
topics.summary: Using a model as a grader, with a rubric, and treating the grader as a system to validate.
learning_objectives: Build a rubric-based grader and run it over a case set
Explain where position and verbosity bias come from
Describe what makes a rubric reproducible

topics.title: Calibrating an LLM Judge
topics.summary: Measuring the judge against human labels before trusting any number it produces.
learning_objectives: Measure judge agreement against your own labels
Report a judged metric with its measured reliability
Explain why an uncalibrated judge score is not evidence

topics.title: Human Evaluations
topics.summary: When a person has to look, how to ask them precisely, and what it costs.
learning_objectives: Design a human evaluation task with unambiguous instructions
Explain what only a human can judge
Sample cases so the result is informative

topics.title: Annotation Quality and Agreement
topics.summary: Two annotators disagreeing means the definition is broken, not that one is wrong.
learning_objectives: Measure agreement between two annotators on the same set
Tighten a definition that produced disagreement
Explain why label noise caps your achievable score

topics.title: Evaluation Metrics for LLM Systems
topics.summary: Choosing metrics that reflect the user's actual goal rather than the easiest thing to count.
learning_objectives: Choose metrics for one real feature and justify each
Explain what a metric cannot see
Combine metrics without hiding a regression

topics.title: Golden Datasets and Dataset Curation
topics.summary: Building the fixed set that defines correct behaviour, and keeping it from going stale.
learning_objectives: Build a golden set from real failures and real traffic shapes
Version it and record how each case was decided
Explain the contamination risk of a leaked golden set

topics.title: Regression Testing for AI Systems
topics.summary: Catching the change that silently breaks what used to work, despite non-determinism.
learning_objectives: Run a regression suite and detect an induced regression
Handle non-determinism without making the test meaningless
Decide what blocks a release and what only warns

topics.title: Offline and Online Evaluation
topics.summary: Measuring before shipping and after shipping, and why offline wins do not always survive.
learning_objectives: Design an offline suite and an online measurement for one change
Explain why an offline gain can vanish in production
Describe a safe online experiment

topics.title: Evaluation Tooling
topics.summary: What the common evaluation libraries provide, and what you already built by hand.
learning_objectives: Reproduce one of your own metrics using an evaluation library
Name what the library standardises and what it assumes
Decide what to keep hand-rolled

topics.title: Tracing and Logging for LLM Systems
topics.summary: A trace per request covering prompts, retrievals, tool calls, tokens and timings.
learning_objectives: Instrument a request end to end and inspect the trace
Explain what a span is and what belongs in one
Decide what must never be stored in a trace

topics.title: Cost and Latency Monitoring
topics.summary: Watching spend and latency per feature continuously, not at the end of the month.
learning_objectives: Build a per-feature cost and latency view
Set an alert threshold from a budget
Explain why token counts must be recorded per request

topics.title: Production Monitoring and Failure Analysis
topics.summary: Detecting quality drift when there is no label, using proxy signals and sampled review.
learning_objectives: Define proxy signals for quality degradation
Sample production traffic for review without violating privacy
Explain how a provider model update can change your behaviour

topics.title: Observability Tooling
topics.summary: What the LLM observability platforms give you beyond your own traces.
learning_objectives: Send traces to an observability tool and query them
Name what the tool adds over your own logging
Describe the data residency question it raises

topics.title: Prompt Injection: Attacks and Defences
topics.summary: Direct and indirect injection, and the layered defences that actually reduce risk.
learning_objectives: Demonstrate direct and indirect injection against your own system
Apply layered defences and show which attacks still succeed
Explain why no prompt-level defence is complete

topics.title: Constraining Inputs and Outputs
topics.summary: Narrowing what can be asked and what can be returned, which is cheaper than detecting misuse.
learning_objectives: Restrict inputs and validate outputs against an allowed set
Explain why a narrow interface is a security control
Add a refusal path with a defined user experience

topics.title: Adversarial Testing and Robust Prompting
topics.summary: Attacking your own system on purpose, and recording what you found.
learning_objectives: Build an adversarial suite and record outcomes
Harden one prompt against a found attack and retest
Explain why adversarial testing is never finished

topics.title: Privacy, Personal Data and User Attribution
topics.summary: Minimising what you send, redacting what you store, and attributing requests to end users.
learning_objectives: Detect and redact personal data before it reaches a provider
Explain why end-user identifiers help abuse handling
State what your system retains and for how long

topics.title: Content Moderation and Abuse Handling
topics.summary: Classifying input and output, and the policy decision behind every threshold.
learning_objectives: Add moderation to an input and output path
Explain the cost of a false positive and a false negative
Describe an escalation path for a flagged case

topics.title: Bias and Fairness
topics.summary: Where bias enters, how to look for it in your own outputs, and what you can and cannot fix.
learning_objectives: Test one system for differential behaviour across groups
Name the stages where bias enters
Explain the limits of a fairness fix at the prompt layer

topics.title: Model Routing, Fallback and Caching
topics.summary: Sending each request to the cheapest model that can do it, and surviving a provider outage.
learning_objectives: Implement routing with a measured quality floor
Add a fallback path and test it by simulating an outage
Measure the hit rate and saving of a response cache

topics.title: Retries, Circuit Breakers and Graceful Degradation
topics.summary: Behaving sensibly when a dependency is slow or gone, instead of amplifying the failure.
learning_objectives: Implement a circuit breaker and demonstrate it opening
Explain how naive retries turn a slowdown into an outage
Define a degraded mode that is still useful

topics.title: Incident Analysis and Error Budgets
topics.summary: Writing up a failure so it does not recur, and spending reliability deliberately.
learning_objectives: Write a blameless incident report for an induced failure
Explain an error budget and what it permits
Convert one incident into a regression test

phases.title: Portfolio, Career and AI-Assisted Development
phases.description: Turning the work into evidence an employer can check, and learning the agentic coding tools last, on purpose, so they amplify understanding instead of replacing it.

topics.title: Project Selection and Scope
topics.summary: Choosing few projects with real depth over many shallow ones, and cutting scope to something finishable.
learning_objectives: Select the projects worth presenting and justify the cut
Define done for one project in measurable terms
Explain why three deep projects beat eight demos

topics.title: Architecture Documentation and Diagrams
topics.summary: A diagram that shows the real mechanism, and prose that names the trade-offs you chose.
learning_objectives: Draw an accurate architecture diagram of one of your systems
Document two trade-offs and the alternative you rejected
Explain the system to a non-specialist in five sentences

topics.title: Metrics-First Project Write-Ups
topics.summary: Leading with what was measured, under what conditions, and what the number does not prove.
learning_objectives: Rewrite one project README to lead with measured results
State the conditions and limitations of every number
Remove every claim you cannot support

topics.title: Reproducible Benchmark Reports
topics.summary: A command anyone can run that reproduces your numbers, including the data and the seed.
learning_objectives: Publish a benchmark that a stranger can reproduce
Record environment, versions and data provenance
Explain run-to-run variance in your own results

topics.title: Clean Repositories and Meaningful Commits
topics.summary: History that reads as a narrative, no secrets, no generated noise, and a working setup path.
learning_objectives: Audit a repository for secrets and generated files
Rewrite a weak commit history into a readable one going forward
Verify setup instructions on a clean machine

topics.title: READMEs, Demos and Deployment Instructions
topics.summary: The first ninety seconds of a reviewer's attention, and what has to happen in them.
learning_objectives: Write a README that gets a stranger running in under ten minutes
Record a short demo that shows the mechanism, not just the output
Provide a deployment path with its real cost

topics.title: AI-Assisted Coding Tools
topics.summary: The agentic coding tools in the official roadmap, learned now that you can review their output.
learning_objectives: Use an agentic coding tool on a real task and review every change
Explain where these tools reliably fail
Describe the review discipline that keeps them safe

topics.title: Using AI Without Outsourcing Your Understanding
topics.summary: The habits that keep a tool from quietly becoming the reason you cannot answer a follow-up question.
learning_objectives: State the rule you will follow for accepting generated code
Explain how to verify an explanation you did not derive
Identify a case where the tool cost you understanding

topics.title: Resume Bullets and Portfolio Presentation
topics.summary: Bullets with numbers and verifiable claims, and a portfolio that leads with the strongest work.
learning_objectives: Write bullets that state action, mechanism and measured result
Remove every unverifiable claim
Order a portfolio by strength rather than chronology

topics.title: Python and AI Coding Interviews
topics.summary: Live problem solving with narration, under time, without a model doing the thinking.
learning_objectives: Solve timed problems while narrating your reasoning
Recover visibly from a wrong first approach
Write tests for your own solution unprompted

topics.title: RAG and Agent Architecture Interviews
topics.summary: Explaining your own systems precisely, including what you measured and what broke.
learning_objectives: Explain a RAG pipeline end to end at a whiteboard level
Defend one design decision and name its cost
Answer what would you do differently honestly

topics.title: AI System Design Rounds
topics.summary: Designing under constraints out loud: requirements, architecture, trade-offs, evaluation, failure modes.
learning_objectives: Design an AI system for a stated requirement in forty minutes
Make cost, latency and reliability trade-offs explicit
Include evaluation and monitoring in the design unprompted

topics.title: Project Deep Dives and Trade-off Explanations
topics.summary: Going three questions deeper than the summary without reaching for the summary again.
learning_objectives: Survive three levels of follow-up on one project
Explain a failure you caused and what you changed
State the limitation an interviewer would find before they do

topics.title: Job Preparation and Technical Communication
topics.summary: Writing and speaking about this work to engineers, managers and non-specialists.
learning_objectives: Explain one system to three different audiences
Write a short technical update that a manager can act on
Ask the questions that reveal whether a role is a fit
